articles.title: There should be black holes in our neighborhood. Can we find them?
articles.source: Phys.org - latest science and technology news stories
articles.summary: Scientific estimates show that there should be between about 100 million and 1 billion stellar-mass black holes in the Milky Way. But they aren't easy to locate. They're not like supermassive black holes (SMBH) at the centers of galaxies. Those are usually easy to spot for different reasons.

articles.title: Curtain-like plasma structures explain solar jets' apparent spinning in simulations
articles.source: Phys.org - latest science and technology news stories
articles.summary: An international team of scientists from the University of Sheffield and the Indian Institute of Astrophysics, led by a postdoctoral research fellow from the University of Newcastle, Australia, has discovered that solar jets called spicules, which are 6–8 Mm long, take the form of warped, denser plasma sheets like pleated drapery.

articles.title: Birds are more afraid of women than men. Scientists have no idea why
articles.summary: Scientists have uncovered a strange pattern in urban bird behavior: Across five European countries and 37 species, birds consistently fled sooner when approached by women than men. articles.title: Oxford scientists discover how viruses build themselves without a blueprint
articles.summary: Scientists have captured virus-like particles assembling themselves step by step, revealing how a surprisingly simple process of trial and error produces complex structures with remarkable precision.
